newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain offers to mediate Colombia talks with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Spain offers to mediate Colombia talks with rebels.

text.p: Colombia said on Tuesday Spain was willing to mediate in any talks it held with the South American country's leading left-wing guerrilla group.
But negotiations would be possible only after the rebels released a number of soldiers held hostage, Colombian Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia told a news conference.
"Spain is willing to help when and how Colombia wants, and assist in striving for the peace that Colombia needs so badly," Mejia said.
"I hope the right conditions will arrive soon, but this requires that the Colombian guerrillas release their 60 hostages," she added.

The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest and oldest rebel force, took a group of soldiers prisoner last August after storming a remote military base in the southwestern Putumayo province.
The exact number taken hostage has varied from 60 to 64 in conflicting accounts by the military and rebels.
Twenty-seven soldiers were also killed in the attack, which marked the start of a nationwide rebel offensive.

"I hope they will release (the hostages) so that we can start to think about the possibility of peace which is still very far away for our country," Mejia said after meeting Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar.
Mejia said the most signficant aspect of her visit to Spain was to "consolidate and reinforce relations".
She said she had discussed the key subject of drug trafficking.
"Colombia is trying to sign agreements regarding judicial cooperation that will strengthen and speed up the fight against drugs," said Mejia.
